name: mushroom alfredo
instructions:
Two variants — variant A is the dairy version (cream cheese OR crème fraîche as the thickening/creaming agent, per the Chris Collins base recipe from Don't Go Bacon My Heart, with refinements folded in). Variant B is an experimental vegan version (blended miso paste + silken tofu) I haven't tested yet. Same technique otherwise; both use pan-fried mushrooms as the load-bearing flavor.

Why this recipe exists in the cookbook: it's a chance to make a creamy italian pasta that doesn't just use a splash of heavy cream — the cream cheese (variant A) or blended silken tofu (variant B) build a genuinely THICK creamy base, not just a rich splash.

=== VARIANT A — DAIRY (CREAM CHEESE OR CRÈME FRAÎCHE) ===

From Chris Collins / Don't Go Bacon My Heart, cream-cheese path — with the going-forward refinements from repeated cooks folded into the procedure below (see notes for the arc). Crème fraîche is a valid substitute for the cream cheese (see notes).

MUSHROOM PICKS: shiitake and oyster are the best default; LIONS MANE is the celebratory option (something special). See notes.

INGREDIENTS (serves 2):
- 7 oz / 200g pasta — tagliatelle OR fettuccine (both work; see PASTA note — fettuccine possibly better)
- 7 oz / 200g mushrooms (shiitake, oyster, or lions mane), sliced
- 3.5 oz / 100g full-fat cream cheese (OR equivalent crème fraîche), at room temp
- 1/2 cup / 120ml chicken stock (for pre-loosening the cream cheese — see procedure)
- 1-2 tsp potato starch (whisked into the cream cheese for sauce stability)
- 1/4 cup / 20g freshly grated parmesan AND 1/4 cup / 20g freshly grated gruyère — BOTH REQUIRED, added at the toss stage. The cream cheese base does NOT replace the finishing cheeses (see CHEESES REQUIRED note). NOT the pre-shredded packet stuff — it doesn't melt right.
- 2 tbsp unsalted BUTTER (not olive oil — see notes)
- 2 cloves garlic, finely diced
- 2 tbsp raw sunflower seeds (sautéed WITH the garlic to toast — see procedure)
- 1/4 cup / 60ml dry white wine (for deglazing the mushrooms — see procedure)
- 1/2 tsp finely diced fresh thyme
- fresh basil, CHIFFONADED (a torn handful, cut into fine ribbons) — added at the end
- salt and black pepper
- reserved pasta water

PROCEDURE:

1. PRE-LOOSEN THE CREAM CHEESE: in a bowl, whisk the cream cheese with the potato starch, then gradually whisk in the chicken stock a splash at a time, building up to a loose, pourable sauce. This is load-bearing (see notes) — the pre-loosened + starch-stabilized base is what makes the sauce integrate cleanly in the pan without blobs.

2. MELT BUTTER in a large pan over medium heat. Add the sliced mushrooms and toss to coat. Spread out so each slice contacts the pan — don't crowd (they'll steam instead of fry). Let them fry undisturbed until golden on the bottom.

3. Meanwhile, start the pasta in well-salted boiling water. DON'T DRAIN the pasta water — you'll need it later.

4. Flip the mushrooms; fry until golden on the other side. Season with salt and pepper. Push mushrooms to the outside of the pan.

5. TOAST SUNFLOWER SEEDS WITH GARLIC IN THE MIDDLE: add garlic AND raw sunflower seeds to the middle of the pan. Fry ~1-2 min — the seeds toast in the butter alongside the garlic. This is the right way to bring the seeds in (not scattered on at the end).

6. DEGLAZE WITH WHITE WINE: pour in the 1/4 cup dry white wine. Let it bubble and reduce by about half, scraping up any browned bits from the pan (~1-2 min). The starch stabilization in the pre-loosened cream cheese base handles the wine acid without breaking the sauce.

7. Turn heat to LOW. Pour in the pre-loosened cream cheese + chicken stock + starch mixture. Stir until the sauce is smooth and integrated with the mushrooms + garlic + toasted seeds.

8. Stir in the fresh thyme.

9. Transfer the cooked pasta straight from the pot to the pan (tongs; carries a little cooking water). Toss to combine. Sprinkle in BOTH the parmesan AND the grated gruyère and continue tossing until the sauce thickens and coats the pasta. Neither cheese is optional — the cream cheese base doesn't replace them (see CHEESES REQUIRED note).

10. Splash in reserved pasta water to thin the sauce as needed. If you overshoot, keep tossing over low heat until it re-thickens.

11. FINISH WITH CHIFFONADED BASIL: torn or chiffonaded fresh basil added at the very end, off heat. Toss once and serve immediately — the sauce thickens fast on the plate.

=== VARIANT B — VEGAN (BLENDED MISO PASTE + SILKEN TOFU) — EXPERIMENTAL, UNTESTED ===

Haven't tried this yet. The idea: replace the cream cheese with a blended base of silken tofu + light miso paste, run through a food processor until smooth. Everything else (mushrooms, garlic, thyme, pasta water, technique) stays the same.

RATIONALE: silken tofu blended smooth gives you the creamy body a cream-cheese sauce provides; miso adds the fermented-tangy depth that cream cheese contributes (cream cheese IS a fermented dairy — silken-tofu-plus-miso approximates the flavor axis, not just the texture). Use the food processor rule from spinach-ricotta (variant B in that recipe) — this whole application uses the same blended-vegan-cheese principle.

Use vegetable stock or mushroom stock alternative for the chicken stock.

Both variants of this recipe want FRESH HERBS — see notes.
notes:
Source: Chris Collins, Don't Go Bacon My Heart — the mushroom tagliatelle recipe. Variant A captured with the refinements from repeated cooks folded into the procedure above. Variant B is my untested extension.

=== MUSHROOM PICKS — SHIITAKE, OYSTER, OR LIONS MANE (CELEBRATORY) ===

Shiitake and oyster are the best defaults — landed on these after trying most varieties (chestnut / baby portobello / cremini / button don't hold up against the cream-cheese-and-thyme axis).

LIONS MANE is the celebratory option — reach for it when you want the dish to feel special. Denser, meatier, more distinctive; carries the sauce beautifully. Not the everyday pick but the right pick for occasions.

Any of the three work well. Mixing shiitake + oyster is also fine.

=== PAN-FRIED MUSHROOMS ARE THE LOAD-BEARING FLAVOR — DON'T CROWD THE PAN ===

Pan-fried mushrooms are the whole savory backbone of both variants. Author's tips (all worth following):
- DON'T WASH THEM: damp cloth to clean. Water adds moisture and steams the fry.
- SPACE THEM OUT: don't cram, they'll steam not fry. Golden-brown surface is the goal.
- DON'T SALT AT THE START: salt draws out moisture. Season AFTER they're golden.
- GARLIC LATER, NOT AT THE START: fry mushrooms first, then push to the side and add garlic briefly.

=== CURRENT REFINED VARIANT A — KEY MOVES (FOLDED INTO PROCEDURE ABOVE) ===

The refinements below are all in the procedure — captured here as the reasoning behind each move.

1. BUTTER, NOT OLIVE OIL. Earlier iteration tried olive oil (thinking butter + cream cheese was too heavy). Walked back — BUTTER is right. The dish wants the butter flavor register alongside the cream cheese. Olive oil pulls it mediterranean; butter keeps it in the northern-italian creamy-pasta tradition Chris Collins built.

2. PRE-LOOSEN THE CREAM CHEESE WITH CHICKEN STOCK + POTATO STARCH BEFORE COOKING. Best way I've found to make a cream cheese sauce: whisk the cream cheese with a dash of POTATO STARCH, then gradually whisk in CHICKEN STOCK (not water — chicken stock is what the sauce actually wants) building up to a loose, pourable sauce texture BEFORE it ever touches the pan. The starch is what lets the sauce hold together when it hits the hot pan; the chicken stock provides both the loosening liquid AND the savory backbone the sauce needs. Prevents cream-cheese blobs in the final pan; the sauce integrates cleanly.

   EARLIER APPROACHES WALKED BACK: (a) loosening with hot water 1 tsp at a time — chicken stock is better. (b) chicken stock deglazing the mushrooms separately, added mid-cook — folding the stock into the pre-loosening step is cleaner and eliminates the earlier confusion about seasoning-during-cook (see below).

3. SUNFLOWER SEEDS SAUTÉED WITH THE GARLIC. Toast the raw sunflower seeds by adding them to the pan WITH the garlic (in the middle of the pan, after the mushrooms are pushed aside). Fry ~1-2 min. This toasts the seeds in the butter and integrates them into the sauce properly. DON'T scatter raw seeds on at the end — they read as raw and disconnected from the dish.

4. NO OLIVE OIL, NO PORCINI POWDER, NO FENNEL, NO ADDITIONAL SEASONINGS REQUIRED. Earlier iterations added porcini powder, red chili flakes, and other seasonings as optional flavor enhancers. Walked back — the base recipe (butter + mushrooms + garlic + sunflower seeds + wine + cream cheese/stock/starch + thyme + basil + PARMESAN + GRUYÈRE) is complete on its own. Adding more crowds it.

5. FENNEL POWDER CLASHES (STILL CLASHING). Confirmed no. Kept in clashing.

6. WHITE WINE VINEGAR — TRIED, WALKED BACK. Not harmful but not doing needed work. Skip it.

7. WHITE WINE DEGLAZE ON THE MUSHROOMS — CONFIRMED, ADOPTED. After the sunflower-seeds-with-garlic step, deglaze with ~1/4 cup dry white wine, reduce by half. The starch stabilization in the pre-loosened cream cheese base handles the wine acid cleanly — the sauce doesn't break. Adds depth that vinegar never did. This is the acid slot the recipe wants, not vinegar.

=== CREAM CHEESE vs CRÈME FRAÎCHE (VARIANT A) ===

Author's default is cream cheese — the cheese aspect mellows out significantly as the sauce comes together, and cream cheese gives you a thicker, more cohesive sauce than a splash of heavy cream would. This is the whole point of the recipe: a creamy italian pasta that's actually THICK-creamy rather than just cream-enriched.

CRÈME FRAÎCHE IS A VALID SUB: crème fraîche is thinner than cream cheese but has a similar cultured-dairy tang. Works if you don't have cream cheese or want a slightly less thick sauce. Same amount (~100g).

Both need to be at ROOM TEMP before starting the pre-loosening step.

=== THE POINT — CREAMY ITALIAN PASTA WITHOUT JUST A SPLASH OF CREAM ===

Most creamy italian pastas cheat via a splash of heavy cream added at the end. This recipe builds actual body via the cream cheese (or crème fraîche) pre-loosened with chicken stock + starch — you get a THICK, cohesive sauce that clings to the pasta properly. The cream-cheese path is what makes it a genuinely creamy dish rather than a cream-enriched one.

Variant B (silken tofu + miso, blended) is the vegan analog of the same principle: build actual sauce body, don't just splash something creamy at the end.

=== FRESH HERBS — THYME + BASIL WELCOME IN BOTH VARIANTS ===

Both variants want fresh herbs:
- THYME: 1/2 tsp finely diced. Load-bearing herb. Added early in the sauce phase.
- BASIL: torn or CHIFFONADED (cut into fine ribbons). Handful, added at the very end off heat. Doesn't wilt too much this way — stays bright green and fresh-tasting.

WANT TO TRY: FRESH MINT (in place of or alongside the basil). Mint pairs cleanly with cream + mushrooms in principle and would push the dish slightly more surprising. Untested.

=== HERB SUBS (AUTHOR'S NOTES) ===

- TARRAGON: works at the same 1/2 tsp quantity as thyme. Stronger, more distinctive flavor — only sub if you like tarragon.
- PARSLEY: milder. Can use up to 2 tsp.
- FRESH ONLY: dried thyme / tarragon / parsley all read wrong here. Fresh matters.

=== CHEESES REQUIRED — PARMESAN + GRUYÈRE, BOTH; CREAM CHEESE BASE DOESN'T REPLACE THEM ===

BOTH FINISHING CHEESES ARE REQUIRED — parmesan AND gruyère, freshly grated, tossed into the pasta at the finishing stage. This is easy to miss because the recipe already has a cream cheese base doing serious dairy work — the temptation is to think 'well, cream cheese is providing the cheese slot, do I really need parmesan + gruyère on top?' You do. The cream cheese does BODY (a thick, spreadable, tangy sauce base). The finishing cheeses do FLAVOR (sharp aged parmesan for salt-and-umami, nutty gruyère for depth and melty pull). They're doing different jobs in the sauce architecture — dropping either leaves a gap.

- PARMESAN: sharp/aged/salty. Cuts through the cream cheese richness. Standard alfredo-tradition cheese.
- GRUYÈRE: nutty, deeply melty, adds a stringy pull as the sauce sets. Distinctive from parmesan — different flavor and different texture contribution.

Both freshly grated. Pre-shredded packet cheese doesn't melt properly — anti-caking additives mess with the sauce texture. Use a microplane or box grater.

VARIANT B (VEGAN): use nutritional yeast alongside the miso to cover the finishing-cheese slot, or just skip (both approaches untested).

=== PASTA WATER TO EMULSIFY THE SAUCE ===

Don't drain the pasta water — reserve a cup. Add splashes to the sauce as you toss with pasta; the starch emulsifies the fats into a smooth glossy sauce. If you overshoot (too watery), keep tossing over low heat and it re-thickens. If you undershoot (too thick), add more.

=== VARIANT B — EXPERIMENTAL, UNTESTED ===

Haven't tried variant B yet. The mental model: substitute the cream cheese slot with blended silken tofu + miso paste (both go in the food processor and get smoothed into a paste before adding to the pan). The tofu provides body, the miso provides fermented-tang and cheesy-ish depth.

Specific quantities untested — probably ~100g silken tofu + 1-2 tsp light miso to start, blend, taste, adjust.

Use vegetable stock or mushroom stock (not chicken stock) for the vegan version.

Same food processor rules apply as in spinach-ricotta variant B: not a blender (Nickelodeon slime problem doesn't apply here since there's no spinach, but the over-smoothing texture problem still does).

=== SUNFLOWER SEEDS CONFIRMED — TOAST WITH GARLIC (LOCKED-IN TECHNIQUE) ===

Raw sunflower seeds sautéed WITH the garlic in the middle of the pan (after mushrooms are pushed aside) — this is the going-forward technique. Toasts them in the butter, integrates into the sauce properly. Don't scatter raw seeds on at the end (earlier iteration tried this; reads disconnected).

SESAME SEEDS: jury still out. Untested at this technique stage — would need to try adding them with the garlic sauté.

PUMPKIN SEEDS: untested. Same technique would probably apply if tried.

=== PASTA — TAGLIATELLE OR FETTUCCINE (FETTUCCINE POSSIBLY BETTER) ===

Walked back the earlier rule ('tagliatelle specifically; flat egg noodles are not a replacement'). Not true — FETTUCCINE works as well or better than tagliatelle in this recipe. Both are flat egg noodles in the same shape family, and fettuccine's slightly narrower ribbons carry the cream cheese sauce cleanly.

Use either. Fettuccine may actually be the better pick.

=== SERVING ===

Serve immediately — the sauce thickens fast once it hits a plate. Author recommends garlic bread on the side.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- spinach-ricotta: uses the same variant A/B dairy-vs-vegan-blend structure. Variant B here (silken tofu + miso blend) uses the same underlying vegan-savory technique as spinach-ricotta variant B (cashews + tofu + miso + nutritional yeast).
- italian-tomato-sauces: the tomato pasta sauce family. This recipe is the cream-based creamy analog — different register, similar 'pasta with a real sauce not just a splash' philosophy.
original_chef: Chris Collins (Don't Go Bacon My Heart).
